items.stem: A read-heavy endpoint is overloading the database. Which change most directly reduces database read load for repeated queries?

options.text: Add a cache in front of the database with an invalidation strategy
options.rationale: Correct: caching repeated reads offloads the database, provided staleness is managed by invalidation.

options.text: Switch the database to synchronous replication
options.rationale: Synchronous replication adds write latency and does not reduce read load.
A longer timeout does not reduce the number of database reads.
Removing the load balancer reduces capacity and availability.

items.explanation: Correct: caching repeated reads offloads the database, provided staleness is managed by invalidation.

items.stem: During a network partition, a system must keep serving requests even if some replicas show slightly stale data. Which tradeoff is being chosen?

options.rationale: Correct: under a partition, serving possibly-stale data favours availability over strong consistency (per CAP).
Choosing consistency would reject requests it cannot serve consistently, reducing availability.
The scenario is about partition behaviour, not durability versus latency.
The described choice concerns read staleness during a partition, not write correctness tradeoffs.

items.explanation: Correct: under a partition, serving possibly-stale data favours availability over strong consistency (per CAP).

items.stem: Which TWO practices improve a system's resilience to downstream failures? (Select TWO)

options.text: Retries with exponential backoff and jitter
options.rationale: Correct: backoff with jitter spreads retries and avoids a synchronized thundering herd.

options.text: Graceful degradation that serves reduced functionality
options.rationale: Correct: degrading gracefully keeps core service available when a dependency fails.

options.text: Unlimited immediate retries on every error
options.rationale: Immediate unbounded retries amplify load and can cause cascading failure.

options.text: Removing all timeouts so calls always wait
options.rationale: No timeouts let failures tie up resources and spread.

items.explanation: Correct: backoff with jitter spreads retries and avoids a synchronized thundering herd.
